capability: Explain Intel HEX sparse address coverage, gaps, entry context and every overlapping write without flashing.
user: Firmware maintainers reviewing a HEX handoff before device programming.
pain: A checksum-valid image can still contain contradictory writes or sparse holes; choosing a last writer hides evidence.
expected: Exit 0: six unique bytes occupy two ranges at 0x08000000..04 and 0x08000008..0A; the interior gap is four bytes. No hole is filled.
contract: ASCII Intel HEX records00/01/02/03/04/05 with actual byte count and checksum validation. Segment and linear base changes affect subsequent records. Ranges use exclusive ends. All overlaps, including identical repeats, are findings; conflicting values have no selected winner. The unambiguous sparse-map SHA256 is domain-separated and hashes sorted four-byte big-endian address plus byte, excluding conflicting cells. Entry records are unique; raw numerical coverage is checked without CPU/A20/Thumb interpretation. EOF is mandatory and final.
limits: 1 MiB,8192 records,262144 data-byte events,32-bit address space. No record may wrap its16-bit offset. Overlap evidence is capped at256 addresses with an omitted count. Gaps are informational. No conversion, winner policy, filling, binary output, flashing or hardware verification.
acceptance: Reproduce mode changes, sparse gaps, checksum errors, identical/conflicting overlaps, address-sensitive hashes, uncovered entries and overflow rejection.
notes: IntelHex and bincopy already parse, merge and convert firmware images; arkku/ihex is a compact C reader/writer. Related overlap and fill discussions are adjacent context, not proof of a current defect. Our report deliberately avoids merge precedence and fill policy.
overlap: This is Intel HEX record addressing and contradictory-write evidence, distinct from the owned generic hexadecimal/text tooling. It is not a renamed formatter or a flasher wrapper.
